fuentes/en-busca-del-tiempo-perdido/resu.texto: Novel in seven volumes narrated in the first person by a man who recalls his childhood and youth in the Parisian high society of the Belle Époque, up to after the First World War. The first volume, Swann's Way, appeared in 1913 from the publisher Grasset, paid for by the author; the last three were published after his death. Its themes are involuntary memory, such as the recollection awakened by the taste of a madeleine dipped in tea, jealousy, snobbery and the passage of time.

fuentes/en-busca-del-tiempo-perdido/por_.texto: It is one of the great models of the modern novel, placing consciousness and memory at the center instead of plot. Proust did not receive the Nobel, but he won the 1919 Prix Goncourt for the second volume.

fuentes/en-busca-del-tiempo-perdido/leer.texto: First volume, Swann's Way, in French (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/ulises/resumen.texto: Novel that follows Leopold Bloom, Stephen Dedalus and Molly Bloom over a single day in Dublin, 16 June 1904, in eighteen episodes that echo Homer's Odyssey. Each episode uses a different style, from interior monologue to drama and parody; the last is Molly's monologue, almost without punctuation. It was serialized in the New York magazine The Little Review from 1918 and published as a book in Paris in 1922 by Sylvia Beach's bookshop Shakespeare and Company.

fuentes/ulises/por_que_importa.texto: It is the central work of English-language modernism and took the interior monologue to its limit. Banned as obscene in the United States and the United Kingdom, a 1933 court ruling allowed it to circulate in the United States; Joyce never received the Nobel.

fuentes/la-metamorfosis/resumen.texto: Story in which Gregor Samsa, a traveling salesman who supports his family, wakes up one morning transformed into a monstrous insect. His family moves from compassion to rejection, and Gregor dies isolated in his room while the others feel relieved. Kafka wrote it in Prague in late 1912 and published it in Leipzig in 1915.

fuentes/la-metamorfosis/por_que_importa.texto: Its opening is one of the best-known sentences in 20th-century literature, and the work helped give meaning to the adjective “Kafkaesque”. It was one of the few works Kafka published during his lifetime.

fuentes/la-metamorfosis/leer.1.titulo.texto: English translation by David Wyllie (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/el-proceso/resumen.texto: Unfinished novel about Josef K., a bank clerk who is arrested one morning without being told what he is accused of and who, over the course of a year, gets lost in an inaccessible court until he is executed. Kafka wrote it in 1914 and 1915 and left it unfinished; Max Brod published it in Berlin in 1925, a year after the author's death, against his request to destroy the manuscripts.

fuentes/el-proceso/por_que_importa.texto: It became the literary image of the individual defenseless before an incomprehensible bureaucracy and justice system, and many later read it as a foreshadowing of totalitarian states.

fuentes/los-buddenbrook/resumen.texto: Novel about four generations of a merchant family from Lübeck, from its peak in 1835 to its extinction. As the artistic sensibility of its members grows, the business and the will to sustain it decline. Mann wrote it between 1897 and 1900, when he was just over twenty, inspired by his own family, and it was published by S. Fischer in Berlin.

fuentes/los-buddenbrook/por_que_importa.texto: It is the great German realist novel of the turn of the century. When Mann received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1929, the committee cited it as the main reason for the award.

fuentes/la-montana-magica/resumen.texto: Hans Castorp, a young engineer from Hamburg, visits his cousin at a tuberculosis sanatorium in Davos, in the Swiss Alps, and stays for seven years. There he listens to the debates between the liberal humanist Settembrini and the radical Jesuit Naphta, who embody the competing ideas of pre-1914 Europe. The novel ends with Castorp on a battlefield of the First World War.

fuentes/la-montana-magica/por_que_import.texto: It is one of the great novels of ideas of the century and a portrait of the Europe that sank into the Great War. Mann began it in 1912 and finished it, greatly expanded, after the war.

fuentes/la-senora-dalloway/resumen.texto: Novel set on a single day in June 1923 in London, while Clarissa Dalloway prepares a party. In parallel it follows Septimus Warren Smith, a First World War veteran with shell shock who ends up taking his own life. Woolf moves from one character's consciousness to another's through interior monologue. It was published by her own press, Hogarth Press.

fuentes/la-senora-dalloway/por_que_impor.texto: It is one of the major examples of the novel of consciousness and one of the first to deal with the trauma of Great War soldiers.

fuentes/el-ruido-y-la-furia/resumen.texto: Novel about the decline of the Compsons, an old planter family of the American South, told in four parts by three brothers and a final narrator. The first part is the voice of Benjy, a man with an intellectual disability who cannot distinguish past from present. The title comes from a monologue in Macbeth: life is “a tale told by an idiot, full of sound and fury”.

fuentes/el-ruido-y-la-furia/por_que_impo.texto: It is Faulkner's most experimental novel and one of the most influential of the century; García Márquez and Onetti acknowledged him as a master. Faulkner received the 1949 Nobel; the committee did not cite a specific work.

fuentes/el-viejo-y-el-mar/titulo.texto: The Old Man and the Sea

fuentes/el-viejo-y-el-mar/resumen.texto: Short narrative about Santiago, an old Cuban fisherman who has gone eighty-four days without catching anything and sets out alone into the Gulf, where he hooks a huge marlin and fights it for almost three days. When he returns, the sharks have eaten his catch and only the skeleton is left. Hemingway wrote it at his home on the outskirts of Havana, and it was published in full in a single issue of Life magazine in September 1952.

fuentes/el-viejo-y-el-mar/por_que_import.texto: It won him the 1953 Pulitzer Prize and was decisive for the 1954 Nobel, whose committee cited it explicitly. It is one of the most widely read stories of the century.

fuentes/rebelion-en-la-granja/resumen.texto: Fable in which the animals of an English farm drive out the owner and found an egalitarian republic, which the pigs end up turning into a dictatorship harsher than the previous one. It is an allegory of the Russian Revolution and Stalinism: the pig Napoleon represents Stalin and Snowball represents Trotsky. Orwell wrote it in 1943 and 1944, but several publishers rejected it so as not to offend the Soviet Union, then an ally.

fuentes/rebelion-en-la-granja/por_que_im.texto: Its line “all animals are equal, but some animals are more equal than others” became proverbial. It was one of the most widely read books of the Cold War.

fuentes/rebelion-en-la-granja/leer.0.tit.texto: English text (Faded Page, public domain in Canada)

fuentes/1984/resumen.texto: Dystopian novel about Winston Smith, an employee of the Ministry of Truth of Oceania, a totalitarian state ruled by the Party and its leader, Big Brother, who watches everyone through telescreens. Winston rewrites the past according to the Party's needs, falls in love with Julia and rebels, until he is arrested and tortured until he loves Big Brother. Orwell wrote it largely on the Scottish island of Jura, already ill with tuberculosis, and published it in London.

fuentes/1984/por_que_importa.texto: It gave the language words such as “Big Brother”, “Newspeak”, “doublethink” and “Orwellian”, and it is the essential reference for discussing surveillance and the manipulation of truth.

fuentes/1984/leer.0.titulo.texto: English text (Faded Page, public domain in Canada)

fuentes/un-mundo-feliz/resumen.texto: Novel that imagines a future world society in which human beings are mass-produced in laboratories, divided into castes, conditioned from childhood and kept happy with consumption, sex without commitment and a drug, soma. The conflict comes with John, a “savage” raised outside that order who reads Shakespeare and rejects that happiness. Huxley wrote it in 1931 in Sanary-sur-Mer, in the south of France, and published it in London in 1932.

fuentes/un-mundo-feliz/por_que_importa.texto: Together with Nineteen Eighty-Four, it is the great dystopia of the century; unlike Orwell, it imagines control based on pleasure rather than fear.

fuentes/fahrenheit-451/resumen.texto: Novel about Guy Montag, a fireman in a future in which firemen do not put out fires but burn books, which are banned by the state. Montag begins reading in secret, flees and joins a group of people who memorize entire books to save them. The title refers to the temperature at which, according to the author, paper burns. Bradbury wrote the first version on a rented typewriter in the basement of the library of the University of California, Los Angeles.

fuentes/fahrenheit-451/por_que_importa.texto: It is one of the reference works against censorship and against the dulling effect of mass media, written at the height of the McCarthy era.

fuentes/el-extranjero/resumen.texto: Novel narrated by Meursault, a clerk in Algiers who attends his mother's funeral with indifference and days later kills an Arab on a beach, almost without motive. At his trial he is sentenced to death less for the crime than for not having wept for his mother. Camus published it in 1942 with Gallimard, in German-occupied Paris.

fuentes/el-extranjero/por_que_importa.texto: It is the novelistic expression of what Camus called the absurd and one of the most widely read French novels of the century. Camus received the 1957 Nobel; the committee did not cite a specific work.

fuentes/la-peste/resumen.texto: Novel about a plague epidemic that ravages the Algerian city of Oran for months, cut off from the world, told by Dr. Rieux, who organizes with others to fight it. Many readers saw it as an allegory of the Nazi occupation of France and the Resistance. It was widely read again during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.

fuentes/la-peste/por_que_importa.texto: It presents solidarity and decency as a response to the absurd and to evil. It was an immediate success and established Camus as one of the central writers of the postwar period.

fuentes/la-nausea/resumen.texto: Novel in the form of a diary by Antoine Roquentin, a historian who lives in Bouville, a port city inspired by Le Havre, and who feels nausea at the brute existence of things, without meaning or necessity. Sartre wrote it while teaching at a lycée in Le Havre and published it with Gallimard in 1938.

fuentes/la-nausea/por_que_importa.texto: It is Sartre's first novel and the literary version of the ideas he later developed in Being and Nothingness. Sartre was chosen for the 1964 Nobel and declined it.

fuentes/doctor-zhivago/resumen.texto: Novel about the physician and poet Yuri Zhivago and his love for Lara, from early 20th-century Russia through the Revolution and the Civil War, which destroy the characters' lives. Rejected in the Soviet Union for its view of the Revolution, the manuscript left the country and was first published in Italian, in Milan, in 1957, by the publisher Giangiacomo Feltrinelli. Zhivago's poems close the book.

fuentes/doctor-zhivago/por_que_importa.texto: Its publication was a Cold War scandal: the CIA secretly financed a Russian-language edition to circulate it in the Soviet bloc. Pasternak received the Nobel in 1958 and, under government pressure, declined it; the novel was not published in the USSR until 1988.

fuentes/el-maestro-y-margarita/resumen.texto: Novel in which the Devil, under the name of Professor Woland, arrives in Soviet Moscow with his retinue, which includes a huge talking cat, and sows chaos among bureaucrats and official writers. In parallel it tells the story of the Master, a persecuted writer who wrote a novel about Pontius Pilate, and of Margarita, who becomes a witch to save him. Bulgakov wrote it between 1928 and 1940 knowing he could not publish it; it appeared in censored form in the magazine Moskva in 1966 and 1967.

fuentes/el-maestro-y-margarita/por_que_i.texto: It is the great satire of Soviet life under Stalin and one of the most widely read Russian novels of the century. Its line “manuscripts don't burn” summed up the faith in the survival of banned literature.

fuentes/un-dia-en-la-vida-de-ivan-deniso.texto: One Day in the Life of Ivan Denisovich

Account of one day in the life of Ivan Denisovich Shukhov, a prisoner in a Soviet labor camp in Kazakhstan, in January 1951, from reveille until he goes to bed. Shukhov was convicted as a spy for having been taken prisoner by the Germans during the war. It was published in November 1962 in the magazine Novy Mir with Khrushchev's personal authorization.
It was the first text legally published in the USSR that depicted Stalin's camps, in the midst of the “Thaw”. It made Solzhenitsyn famous worldwide and paved the way for his 1970 Nobel.

fuentes/archipielago-gulag/resumen.texto: History of the Soviet Union's system of forced labor camps between 1918 and 1956, built from the author's experience and the testimonies of 227 former prisoners. It describes the arrests, interrogations, transports, and life and death in the camps. Solzhenitsyn wrote it in secret between 1958 and 1968; when the KGB found a copy in 1973, he decided to publish it in Paris, and the following year he was expelled from the USSR.

fuentes/archipielago-gulag/por_que_impor.texto: It changed the view of the Soviet Union in the West, especially among French left-wing intellectuals. Historians dispute some of its victim figures, but the archives opened in the 1990s confirmed its overall picture.

fuentes/si-esto-es-un-hombre/resumen.texto: Primo Levi's testimony about his deportation and the nearly one year he spent in Monowitz, the Auschwitz labor camp, from February 1944 until the liberation in January 1945. With a chemist's precision, it describes the destruction of the prisoners' dignity and the logic of the camp. Rejected by the publisher Einaudi, it was published by a small Turin publisher in 1947; the 1958 Einaudi edition made it well known.

fuentes/si-esto-es-un-hombre/por_que_imp.texto: It is one of the fundamental testimonies of the Holocaust and is read in schools throughout Europe.

fuentes/diario-de-ana-frank/resumen.texto: Diary that Anne Frank wrote between the ages of 13 and 15, from June 1942 to August 1944, while hiding with her family and four other people in a secret annex of a building in Amsterdam, then occupied by the Nazis. It describes the daily life of confinement, the conflicts of living together and her own growing up; she herself began rewriting it for publication after the war. Her father, Otto Frank, the group's only survivor, published it in 1947.

fuentes/diario-de-ana-frank/por_que_impo.texto: It is the most widely read book about the Holocaust and gave its victims a face and a voice.

fuentes/la-noche-wiesel/resumen.texto: Autobiographical account of the deportation of Elie Wiesel, at fifteen, with his family, from Sighet to Auschwitz in 1944, and of the death march to Buchenwald, where his father died in January 1945, a few months before the liberation. A longer version appeared in Yiddish in Buenos Aires in 1956 under the title And the World Remained Silent; the shorter French version was published in Paris in 1958 with a foreword by François Mauriac.

fuentes/la-noche-wiesel/por_que_importa.texto: Along with Primo Levi's, it is one of the most widely read testimonies of the Holocaust, and the text that made Wiesel a public voice for the memory of the genocide.

fuentes/todo-se-desmorona/resumen.texto: Novel about Okonkwo, a respected warrior from an Igbo village in what is now southeastern Nigeria in the late 19th century, and the disintegration of his world with the arrival of missionaries and the British colonial administration. Achebe describes from within the customs, beliefs and conflicts of Igbo society. The title comes from a poem by W. B. Yeats.

fuentes/todo-se-desmorona/por_que_import.texto: It is the most widely read African novel in the world and the starting point of modern African literature in English, written as a response to the image of Africa in European colonial novels.

fuentes/trilogia-de-el-cairo/resumen.texto: Three novels, Palace Walk, Palace of Desire and Sugar Street, that follow three generations of the family of the merchant Ahmad Abd al-Jawad in a neighborhood of old Cairo, from 1917, on the eve of the 1919 revolution against the British, to 1944. They portray the changes in Egyptian society: nationalism, the status of women, religion, communism and the Muslim Brotherhood. Mahfouz finished it around 1952 and published it in 1956 and 1957.

fuentes/trilogia-de-el-cairo/por_que_imp.texto: It is the major work of the modern Arabic novel. Mahfouz received the 1988 Nobel, the first for an author writing in Arabic; the committee highlighted his work as a whole.

fuentes/gitanjali/resumen.texto: Book of devotional poems, close to the bhakti tradition, addressed to a divinity at once intimate and universal. The Bengali version appeared in 1910; in 1912 Tagore published in London his own English translation in poetic prose, Song Offerings, with a preface by W. B. Yeats, which also included poems from his other books.

fuentes/gitanjali/por_que_importa.texto: It earned him the 1913 Nobel Prize in Literature, the first for a non-European author: the committee highlighted his verse written “in his own English words”, that is, this translation. In Spanish it was translated by Zenobia Camprubí and Juan Ramón Jiménez as Ofrenda lírica.

fuentes/pais-de-nieve/resumen.texto: Novel about the relationship between Shimamura, a wealthy dilettante from Tokyo, and Komako, a geisha at a hot-spring resort in a snowy mountain area on the Sea of Japan side. Kawabata published it in installments from 1935 and gave it its final form in 1948. It is told in brief, elliptical scenes, close to haiku.

fuentes/pais-de-nieve/por_que_importa.texto: It is his best-known novel; the 1968 Nobel presentation speech mentioned it together with Thousand Cranes and The Old Capital. It introduced the West to a Japanese aesthetic of suggestion and melancholy.

fuentes/el-senor-de-los-anillos/resumen.texto: Fantasy novel, a sequel to The Hobbit, about the hobbit Frodo Baggins's mission to destroy the One Ring of the dark lord Sauron in the fire of Mount Doom, in the imaginary world of Middle-earth. Tolkien wrote it between 1937 and 1949, with invented languages, history and maps, and the publisher Allen & Unwin released it in three volumes in 1954 and 1955.

fuentes/el-senor-de-los-anillos/por_que_.texto: It founded modern fantasy as a genre and is one of the best-selling novels in history. Tolkien denied that it was an allegory of the Second World War, although his experience in the First left its mark on the book.

fuentes/lolita/resumen.texto: Novel narrated by Humbert Humbert, a European professor who, from prison, tells how he abused Dolores Haze, a twelve-year-old girl, for two years while traveling with her through the motels of the United States. The narrator tries to seduce the reader with his prose, while the story reveals the harm he causes. Rejected by American publishers, it was published in Paris in 1955 by Olympia Press and in the United States in 1958.

fuentes/lolita/por_que_importa.texto: It is one of the masterpieces of English prose style and a celebrated case in the debate over literature, morality and censorship. The protagonist's name entered common usage with a meaning that inverts that of the book, in which she is the victim.

fuentes/la-tierra-baldia/resumen.texto: Poem of 434 lines in five parts that layers voices, quotations in several languages and ancient myths to depict a civilization in ruins after the First World War. Ezra Pound cut the manuscript heavily. It was published in October 1922 in the London magazine The Criterion, edited by Eliot himself.

fuentes/la-tierra-baldia/por_que_importa.texto: It is the most influential poem of English-language modernism. Eliot received the 1948 Nobel; the committee did not cite a specific work.

fuentes/esperando-a-godot/resumen.texto: Play in two acts in which two tramps, Vladimir and Estragon, wait beside a tree for someone called Godot who never arrives, while they talk, argue and encounter the master Pozzo and his slave Lucky. Beckett wrote it in French between 1948 and 1949; it was published in 1952 and premiered in Paris in January 1953. He translated it into English himself.

fuentes/esperando-a-godot/por_que_import.texto: It is the best-known work of the so-called Theatre of the Absurd and changed 20th-century playwriting. Beckett received the 1969 Nobel; the committee did not cite a specific work.

fuentes/las-uvas-de-la-ira/resumen.texto: Novel about the Joads, a family of Oklahoma farmers who lose their land during the Great Depression and the dust storms of the Dust Bowl and travel to California in search of work, where they find exploitation and hunger. It alternates chapters of the family's story with general chapters about the migration. It was the best-selling book of 1939 and won the Pulitzer Prize in 1940.

fuentes/las-uvas-de-la-ira/por_que_impor.texto: It is the great literary portrait of the Great Depression in the United States; it was banned and burned in some counties for its portrayal of landowners. Steinbeck received the 1962 Nobel Prize; the committee did not cite any particular work.

fuentes/siddhartha/resumen.texto: Short novel about Siddhartha, the son of a Brahmin in the India of the Buddha's time, who leaves home in search of enlightenment: he passes through the ascetics, listens to Gotama Buddha, lives as a wealthy merchant and ends up learning from a river and a ferryman. Hesse wrote it after a journey through Ceylon and Southeast Asia in 1911 and a long study of Buddhism and Hinduism.

fuentes/siddhartha/por_que_importa.texto: It was one of the most widely read books of the 1960s counterculture and brought millions of Western readers an image of Indian thought. Hesse received the 1946 Nobel Prize; the committee did not cite any particular work.

fuentes/sin-novedad-en-el-frente/titulo.texto: All Quiet on the Western Front

fuentes/sin-novedad-en-el-frente/resumen.texto: Novel narrated by Paul Bäumer, a German student who enlists with his classmates, urged on by a patriotic teacher, and lives through trench warfare on the Western Front. One by one his friends die, and Paul falls in October 1918, on a day so quiet that the army report says only “all quiet on the Western Front”. It was serialized in the newspaper Vossische Zeitung in 1928 and published as a book in 1929.

fuentes/sin-novedad-en-el-frente/por_que.texto: It is the most widely read novel about the First World War. The Nazis considered it defeatist: they burned it in 1933 and banned the book and its film version.

fuentes/beloved/resumen.texto: Novel about Sethe, a woman who escaped slavery in Kentucky and lives in Cincinnati in 1873, haunted by the ghost of the daughter she herself killed so that she would not be returned to slavery. Morrison based it on the real case of Margaret Garner, from 1856.

fuentes/beloved/por_que_importa.texto: It won the Pulitzer Prize in 1988 and is one of the most important novels about the memory of slavery in the United States. Morrison received the 1993 Nobel Prize; the committee did not cite any particular work.

fuentes/ensayo-sobre-la-ceguera/resumen.texto: Novel in which an epidemic of white blindness spreads through an unnamed city. The government confines the first victims in an asylum, where life together degenerates into violence and abuse; only a doctor's wife keeps her sight and guides a small group. The characters have no names and the dialogue has no quotation marks, as in the rest of Saramago's work.

fuentes/ensayo-sobre-la-ceguera/por_que_.texto: It is his best-known novel, an allegory about the fragility of civilization. Saramago received the 1998 Nobel Prize “for his parables sustained by imagination, compassion and irony”.

fuentes/romancero-gitano/resumen.texto: Book of eighteen romances, the traditional form of Spanish popular poetry, which blend the world of the Andalusian Gypsies with avant-garde imagery, myths and an ever-present death. It includes the “Somnambule Ballad” (“Green, how I want you green”) and the “Ballad of the Spanish Civil Guard”. It was published by the Revista de Occidente in Madrid in 1928.

fuentes/romancero-gitano/por_que_importa.texto: It was an immediate success and is one of the most widely read books of Spanish-language poetry of the century.

fuentes/los-versos-satanicos/resumen.texto: Novel about two Indian actors who fall from the sky when a hijacked plane explodes over the English Channel and are transformed, one into an angel and the other into a devil, in the immigrant London. It includes dreamlike episodes about a prophet named Mahound, inspired by the life of Muhammad and by the account, transmitted by some early Muslim historians, of verses the Prophet supposedly recited at Satan's prompting and later withdrew. Many Muslims considered it blasphemous.

fuentes/los-versos-satanicos/por_que_imp.texto: In February 1989 Ayatollah Khomeini issued a fatwa calling for the killing of Rushdie and his publishers, and the Japanese translator was murdered in 1991. The case became the great end-of-century debate on freedom of expression and blasphemy.

fuentes/hijos-de-la-medianoche/resumen.texto: Novel narrated by Saleem Sinai, born at midnight on 15 August 1947, at the moment of India's independence, and endowed, like the other children born in that hour, with magical powers. His life intertwines with the history of the country from 1915 to Indira Gandhi's state of emergency (1975–1977).

fuentes/hijos-de-la-medianoche/por_que_i.texto: It won the 1981 Booker Prize and in 1993 and 2008 was chosen as the best novel among all the winners. It is a central example of the postcolonial novel and of magical realism outside Latin America.

fuentes/la-vegetariana/resumen.texto: Novel in three parts about Yeong-hye, a woman from Seoul who, after a dream, stops eating meat, and the violent reaction of her husband, her father and her family to that refusal, which ends with her psychiatric confinement. Each part takes the point of view of a different character: the husband, the brother-in-law and the sister.

fuentes/la-vegetariana/por_que_importa.texto: Its English translation won the 2016 International Booker Prize and made Han Kang known around the world. She received the 2024 Nobel Prize “for her intense poetic prose that confronts historical traumas and exposes the fragility of human life”.

fuentes/voces-de-chernobil/resumen.texto: Book made up of the testimonies of hundreds of people affected by the accident at the Chernobyl nuclear power plant in 1986: firefighters' widows, liquidators, evacuees, scientists, soldiers and officials. Alexievich, who lived in Belarus, the most contaminated country, interviewed them over ten years and presents them with almost no intervention.

fuentes/voces-de-chernobil/por_que_impor.texto: It is the best-known work of a genre she called the “novel of voices”. She received the 2015 Nobel Prize “for her polyphonic writings, a monument to suffering and courage in our time”.

fuentes/me-llamo-rojo/resumen.texto: Detective and historical novel set in Istanbul in 1591, among the Ottoman sultan's miniaturists, who are secretly commissioned to produce an illustrated book in the style of the Venetian painters. When one of them is found murdered, the investigation reveals the clash between the Islamic tradition of miniature painting and the perspective of the European Renaissance. Each chapter is narrated by a different voice, among them a corpse, a dog, a coin and the color red.

fuentes/me-llamo-rojo/por_que_importa.texto: It won the International IMPAC Dublin Literary Award in 2003 and is one of his most translated novels. Pamuk received the 2006 Nobel Prize; the committee highlighted his quest for the “melancholic soul of his native city”.

fuentes/la-insoportable-levedad-del-ser/.texto: Novel about two couples, the surgeon Tomas and the photographer Tereza, and the painter Sabina and her lover Franz, in the Czechoslovakia of the Prague Spring and the Soviet invasion of 1968. It blends history with philosophical reflections on the weight and lightness of life, starting from Nietzsche's eternal return. It was published first in French, in Paris, in 1984, and in Czech in Toronto in 1985, because it was banned in his country.
It was a worldwide success that showed Western readers life under communist “normalization”; Philip Kaufman adapted it for the screen in 1988.

fuentes/los-anos-ernaux/resumen.texto: Impersonal autobiography that tells the author's life from her birth, in 1940, to 2006, together with the history of French society in those decades, using not “I” but “she” and “we”. It is built from photos, songs, advertisements, set phrases and collective memories of each period.

fuentes/los-anos-ernaux/por_que_importa.texto: It is considered her major work. Ernaux received the 2022 Nobel Prize “for the courage and clinical acuity with which she uncovers the roots, estrangements and collective restraints of personal memory”.

fuentes/satantango/resumen.texto: Novel about the inhabitants of a ruined collective farm on the Hungarian plain who, under incessant rain, await Irimiás, a man they believed dead who promises to save them, although he works as a police informer. Its twelve chapters move forward and back like the steps of a tango, in extremely long sentences.

fuentes/satantango/por_que_importa.texto: It is his first and best-known novel, adapted for the screen by Béla Tarr in 1994 in a film more than seven hours long. Krasznahorkai received the 2025 Nobel Prize “for his compelling and visionary oeuvre that, in the midst of apocalyptic terror, reaffirms the power of art”.

fuentes/ficciones/resumen.texto: Short-story collection that brings together The Garden of Forking Paths (1941) and Artifices (1944), with stories such as “Tlön, Uqbar, Orbis Tertius”, “Pierre Menard, Author of the Quixote”, “The Lottery in Babylon”, “The Library of Babel” and “Funes the Memorious”. It blends the detective and fantastic story with the essay, invented erudition and philosophy. It was published by the Sur publishing house.

fuentes/ficciones/por_que_importa.texto: It is the book that made Borges a world author, especially after the 1961 Formentor Prize, shared with Beckett. Critics saw in it an anticipation of ideas of postmodernity and of information networks.

fuentes/el-aleph/resumen.texto: Short-story collection published by Losada that includes “The Immortal”, “Emma Zunz”, “Deutsches Requiem”, “The House of Asterion”, “The Zahir” and “The Aleph”, in which the narrator, named Borges, discovers in a cellar on Garay Street a point that contains all the points of the universe. Its themes are time, eternity, identity and the infinite.

fuentes/el-aleph/por_que_importa.texto: Together with Ficciones, it is Borges's central work and one of the summits of the Spanish-language short story.

fuentes/rayuela/resumen.texto: Novel about Horacio Oliveira, an Argentine who lives in Paris among the artists and intellectuals of the “Serpent Club” and loves La Maga, and who later returns to Buenos Aires. Its “table of instructions” proposes two ways of reading it: straight through to chapter 56, or jumping between chapters in an order that includes the “expendable chapters”. Cortázar wrote it in Paris and it was published by the Sudamericana publishing house of Buenos Aires in 1963.

fuentes/rayuela/por_que_importa.texto: It was the novel of a generation of young readers in the 1960s and one of the works that opened the Latin American Boom, through its experimentation with the form of the novel.

fuentes/el-tunel/resumen.texto: Short novel narrated from prison by the painter Juan Pablo Castel, who confesses to having killed María Iribarne, the only person who seemed to understand his painting. His obsessive account of jealousy and loneliness takes place in Buenos Aires and on an estancia on the coast. It was published by the Sur publishing house in 1948.

fuentes/el-tunel/por_que_importa.texto: It was praised by Albert Camus, who recommended it to the Gallimard publishing house, and is one of the most widely read existentialist novels in Spanish.

fuentes/sobre-heroes-y-tumbas/resumen.texto: Novel about the love of Martín, a young porteño, for Alejandra Vidal Olmos, the daughter of a declining patrician family, in the Buenos Aires of 1953 to 1955. It includes the “Report on the Blind” by Fernando, Alejandra's father, a delirium about a sect that rules the world, and General Lavalle's retreat to the north in 1841, after the Unitarian defeat.

fuentes/sobre-heroes-y-tumbas/por_que_im.texto: It is Sabato's most ambitious novel and one of the great novels about Argentine identity, with Peronism and its fall as a backdrop.

fuentes/la-invencion-de-morel/resumen.texto: Short novel in the form of the diary of a Venezuelan fugitive who takes refuge on a deserted island and discovers a group of tourists who repeat the same gestures and dialogues every week; he falls in love with one of them, Faustine, who does not seem to see him. He discovers that they are three-dimensional images recorded by a machine invented by Morel, which eternally reproduces the people it has recorded. Borges wrote its prologue and did not hesitate to call it “perfect”.

fuentes/la-invencion-de-morel/por_que_im.texto: It is a classic of Spanish-language science fiction and fantasy, which many read as an anticipation of virtual reality.

fuentes/los-siete-locos/resumen.texto: Novel about Remo Erdosain, a bill collector accused of stealing from his company, humiliated and anguished, who joins the Astrologer, a character who plans a secret society to seize power, financed by brothels and mixing ideas from fascism and Bolshevism. It continues in The Flamethrowers (1931).

fuentes/los-siete-locos/por_que_importa.texto: It is one of the founding novels of modern Argentine urban fiction, and many critics saw in it an anticipation of the climate of the 1930 coup.

fuentes/desolacion/resumen.texto: Gabriela Mistral's first book of poems, published in New York by the Instituto de las Españas at the initiative of the Hispanist Federico de Onís. It includes the “Sonnets of Death”, awarded a prize in Santiago in 1914, and poems about motherhood, school and the landscape.

fuentes/desolacion/por_que_importa.texto: It made her known throughout the Hispanic world. In 1945 she received the Nobel Prize, the first in Literature for Latin America, “for her lyric poetry which, inspired by powerful emotions, has made her name a symbol of the idealistic aspirations of the entire Latin American world”.

fuentes/el-senor-presidente/resumen.texto: Novel about the dictatorship of an unnamed president in an unnamed country, inspired by the rule of Manuel Estrada Cabrera in Guatemala (1898–1920). After the murder of a colonel, the president uses the crime to persecute his enemies, in a climate of fear, denunciation and cruelty narrated in dreamlike imagery. Asturias wrote it mainly in Paris between the 1920s and the early 1930s and published it in Mexico in 1946.

fuentes/el-senor-presidente/por_que_impo.texto: It is one of the first great dictator novels, a central theme of Latin American literature. Asturias received the 1967 Nobel Prize for a literature “rooted in the national traits and traditions of the indigenous peoples of Latin America”.

fuentes/canto-general/resumen.texto: Book of fifteen sections and more than two hundred poems that traces the history of the Americas from nature and the pre-Columbian peoples through the conquest, the wars of independence and the workers' struggles of the 20th century. Its most famous section is “The Heights of Macchu Picchu”. Neruda wrote it partly in hiding, persecuted by the government of González Videla, and published it in Mexico in 1950 with illustrations by Diego Rivera and David Alfaro Siqueiros.

fuentes/canto-general/por_que_importa.texto: It is the great poetic epic of 20th-century Latin America, written from a communist perspective. Neruda received the 1971 Nobel Prize “for a poetry that with the action of an elemental force brings alive a continent's destiny and dreams”.

fuentes/pedro-paramo/resumen.texto: Novel in which Juan Preciado goes to Comala to look for his father, Pedro Páramo, a cacique who dominated the region, and finds a town inhabited by talking dead. Through fragments and murmurs the story of the cacique is reconstructed, along with his love for Susana San Juan and the ruin of the town, from the Porfiriato to the Cristero War. It was published by the Fondo de Cultura Económica in 1955.

fuentes/pedro-paramo/por_que_importa.texto: It is one of the most influential Spanish-language novels of the century: García Márquez said he came to know it by heart and that it showed him the way to write One Hundred Years of Solitude.

fuentes/cien-anos-de-soledad/resumen.texto: Novel about seven generations of the Buendía family in Macondo, an imaginary town on the Colombian Caribbean coast, from its founding to its disappearance. It blends the marvelous and the everyday with the history of Colombia: the civil wars between Liberals and Conservatives, the arrival of the banana company and the 1928 massacre of strikers. García Márquez wrote it in Mexico City in 1965 and 1966, and it was published by the Sudamericana publishing house of Buenos Aires in 1967.

fuentes/cien-anos-de-soledad/por_que_imp.texto: It is the best-known novel of magical realism and of the Latin American Boom, with tens of millions of copies sold. García Márquez received the 1982 Nobel Prize “for his novels and short stories, in which the fantastic and the realistic are combined in a richly composed world of imagination”.

fuentes/la-ciudad-y-los-perros/resumen.texto: Novel about a group of cadets at the Leoncio Prado Military Academy in Lima, where the author himself studied, and about the violence, racism and corruption of the institution, starting from the theft of an exam and the death of a cadet. It won the Premio Biblioteca Breve of the Seix Barral publishing house, which published it in Barcelona in 1963.

fuentes/la-ciudad-y-los-perros/por_que_i.texto: It was Vargas Llosa's first novel and one of those that inaugurated the Latin American Boom. He received the 2010 Nobel Prize “for his cartography of structures of power and his images of the individual's resistance, revolt, and defeat”.

fuentes/el-laberinto-de-la-soledad/resum.texto: Essay on Mexican identity that starts from the “pachucos”, young people of Mexican origin in Los Angeles, and goes through masks, fiestas, death, the figure of La Malinche and the history of the country, from the conquest to the Revolution. Paz wrote it in Paris, while working at the Mexican embassy, and it was published by Cuadernos Americanos in Mexico in 1950.

fuentes/el-laberinto-de-la-soledad/por_q.texto: It is the most influential essay on Mexican national identity. Paz received the 1990 Nobel Prize “for impassioned writing with wide horizons, characterized by sensuous intelligence and humanistic integrity”.

fuentes/ariel/resumen.texto: Essay in the form of a speech by an old teacher, Prospero, to his students at the end of the school year, beside a statue of Ariel, the spirit from Shakespeare's The Tempest. He urges them to cultivate the spirit, beauty and disinterestedness against utilitarianism, which he identifies with the United States, and advises against imitating the North American model, which he calls “nordomanía”.

fuentes/ariel/por_que_importa.texto: It was the most influential text among Spanish American youth in the early 20th century and gave its name to “Arielism”. It appeared in Montevideo in 1900, two years after the war between Spain and the United States.

fuentes/la-raza-cosmica/resumen.texto: Essay in which Vasconcelos argues that the mixing of races in Latin America will give rise to a fifth race, the “cosmic race”, which will synthesize all the others and open an era of the spirit. It includes notes from his official trip to Brazil and Argentina in 1922, when he was Secretary of Public Education.

fuentes/la-raza-cosmica/por_que_importa.texto: It was one of the main defenses of mestizaje as the basis of Latin American identity, against the scientific racism of the time. Its critics point out that it retains racial hierarchies and devalues Indigenous and Black peoples.

fuentes/el-hombre-mediocre/resumen.texto: Essay on psychology and morals that contrasts the mediocre man, who adapts to the routine and opinions of his time, with the idealist, who pursues perfection and pushes society forward. Ingenieros wrote it in Europe, where he went in 1911 after President Roque Sáenz Peña did not appoint him professor of legal medicine even though he headed the shortlist, and it was published by the Renacimiento publishing house of Madrid and Buenos Aires.

fuentes/el-hombre-mediocre/por_que_impor.texto: It was one of the books most widely read by Latin American youth for decades and one of the inspirations of the 1918 University Reform movement.

fuentes/la-rebelion-de-las-masas/resumen.texto: Essay describing the irruption of the “mass man” into European public life: a self-satisfied average man who believes he is entitled to everything without obligations or respect for the minorities that create culture. Ortega sees Bolshevism and fascism as two expressions of that revolt and proposes the unity of Europe as a way out. It appeared in installments in the newspaper El Sol in 1929 and as a book in 1930.

fuentes/la-rebelion-de-las-masas/por_que.texto: It is one of the most translated Spanish-language works of thought of the century, read with special attention in Argentina. Its critics consider it an elitist defense against mass democracy.

fuentes/la-interpretacion-de-los-suenos/.texto: Book in which Freud argues that dreams are the disguised fulfillment of repressed wishes and that they can be interpreted with the method of free association. He analyzes many of his own dreams and those of his patients, presents a model of the psychic apparatus with the unconscious, and sets out for the first time the idea he later called the Oedipus complex. It appeared in November 1899, but the publisher dated it 1900.
It is the founding work of psychoanalysis, which changed psychiatry, literature, art and the everyday language of the 20th century; its scientific status has been debated ever since.

fuentes/investigaciones-logicas/resumen.texto: Work in two volumes. The first criticizes psychologism, the idea that the laws of logic are laws of human psychology; the second analyzes meaning and the experiences of consciousness, with the notion of intentionality: all consciousness is consciousness of something.

fuentes/investigaciones-logicas/por_que_.texto: It is the work with which phenomenology was born, the movement that Heidegger, Sartre and Merleau-Ponty each followed in their own way.

fuentes/principia-mathematica/resumen.texto: Three-volume work by Alfred North Whitehead and Bertrand Russell that attempts to derive all of mathematics from a small number of logical principles, using its own symbolic language. To avoid the paradoxes of set theory, such as the one Russell had discovered in 1901, it introduces the theory of types. The proof that 1 + 1 = 2 comes only after hundreds of pages.

fuentes/principia-mathematica/por_que_im.texto: It was the foundation of modern mathematical logic and of analytic philosophy. In 1931 Kurt Gödel proved that no system of that kind can prove all the truths of arithmetic.

fuentes/tractatus/resumen.texto: Short book of numbered propositions which holds that language is a logical picture of the world and that only propositions describing facts have sense; the ethical, the aesthetic and the mystical cannot be said, only shown. It ends with “Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent”. Wittgenstein finished it in 1918, as an Austrian soldier, and published it in German in 1921 and in a bilingual edition in London in 1922, with a preface by Russell.

fuentes/tractatus/por_que_importa.texto: It had a decisive influence on the Vienna Circle and logical positivism, and is one of the founding texts of analytic philosophy.

fuentes/investigaciones-filosoficas/resu.texto: Posthumous work in which Wittgenstein abandons the Tractatus idea that language reflects the logical form of the world: the meaning of a word is its use in the “language games” of a form of life. It includes the argument against the possibility of a private language. Wittgenstein prepared it between 1936 and 1949, and it was published in 1953, in a bilingual German and English edition, two years after his death.

fuentes/investigaciones-filosoficas/por_.texto: It is one of the most influential works of 20th-century philosophy and inspired ordinary language philosophy.

fuentes/ser-y-tiempo/resumen.texto: Work that takes up again the question of the meaning of being through an analysis of the human being, which it calls Dasein (“being-there”): someone thrown into the world, who deals with things, lives in the impersonality of the “they” and faces their own death. Temporality appears as the meaning of that existence. Heidegger published it unfinished in 1927, in Husserl’s yearbook of phenomenology, and dedicated it to him.

fuentes/ser-y-tiempo/por_que_importa.texto: It is one of the most influential works of 20th-century philosophy and a starting point for existentialism, hermeneutics and deconstruction. Its reading is shaped by the debate over Heidegger’s support for Nazism.

fuentes/el-ser-y-la-nada/resumen.texto: Treatise of “phenomenological ontology” that distinguishes the being-in-itself of things from the being-for-itself of consciousness, which is freedom and nothingness. The human being is “condemned to be free” and is responsible for what they make of themselves; “bad faith” is the self-deception by which that freedom is denied. Sartre published it in 1943, in occupied Paris.

fuentes/el-ser-y-la-nada/por_que_importa.texto: It is the central philosophical work of French existentialism, which shaped postwar culture.

fuentes/el-existencialismo-es-un-humanis.texto: Lecture that Sartre gave on 29 October 1945 in Paris before a large crowd, published in 1946, to defend existentialism against criticism from communists and Catholics. It sums up his philosophy in the formula “existence precedes essence”: there is no given human nature, and each person makes themselves through their actions, choosing at the same time for all of humanity.
It is the most widely read introduction to existentialism, although Sartre himself later regretted having published it because of its simplifications.

fuentes/el-mito-de-sisifo/resumen.texto: Essay that starts from the question of whether life is worth living in the face of the absurd, the clash between the human desire for meaning and the silence of the world. Camus rejects suicide and the religious “leap” and proposes living the absurd with revolt, freedom and passion. It ends with Sisyphus, condemned to push a rock uphill for eternity: “one must imagine Sisyphus happy”.

fuentes/el-mito-de-sisifo/por_que_import.texto: It is the philosophical basis of Camus’s literary work and one of the most widely read essays of the century.

fuentes/la-estructura-de-las-revolucione.texto: Book that describes the history of science as an alternation between periods of “normal science”, in which problems are solved within an accepted paradigm, and scientific revolutions, such as those of Copernicus, Newton or Einstein, in which accumulated anomalies lead to a change of paradigm. It holds that successive paradigms are partly incommensurable. It was published in 1962 in a University of Chicago series.

It popularized the words “paradigm” and “paradigm shift” and is one of the most cited academic books of the century. It was criticized by, among others, Karl Popper and his students for opening the door to relativism.

fuentes/vigilar-y-castigar/resumen.texto: Study of the shift from public torture, such as the execution of Damiens in 1757, to the modern prison, between the late 18th century and 1840. Foucault argues that the prison is part of a disciplinary power that watches, classifies and normalizes people also in schools, barracks, factories and hospitals, and takes as its model Jeremy Bentham’s panopticon.

fuentes/vigilar-y-castigar/por_que_impor.texto: It is one of the most cited books in the humanities and social sciences and renewed the study of power, punishment and surveillance. Some historians objected to its poorly documented generalizations.

fuentes/teoria-de-la-justicia/resumen.texto: Treatise of political philosophy that asks which principles of justice free and equal persons would choose in an “original position”, behind a “veil of ignorance” that prevents them from knowing what place they will occupy in society. Rawls argues that they would choose equal basic liberties for all and would accept economic inequalities only if they benefit the least advantaged (the “difference principle”).

fuentes/teoria-de-la-justicia/por_que_im.texto: It renewed English-language political philosophy and is the foundation of egalitarian liberalism. Its best-known critique came from Robert Nozick in Anarchy, State, and Utopia (1974).

fuentes/de-la-gramatologia/resumen.texto: Book in which Derrida criticizes what he calls logocentrism, the Western tradition that privileges speech as the presence of meaning and treats writing as a mere supplement. He analyzes texts by Saussure, Lévi-Strauss and Rousseau to show that writing and difference lie at the very origin of language.

fuentes/de-la-gramatologia/por_que_impor.texto: It is the founding text of deconstruction, which shaped literary theory and cultural studies from the 1970s on. Its critics, above all in analytic philosophy, consider it obscure.

fuentes/teoria-de-la-accion-comunicativa.texto: Two-volume work that distinguishes strategic action, oriented to success, from communicative action, oriented to understanding through arguments that everyone can accept. Habermas argues that modernity tends toward the “colonization of the lifeworld” by the systems of money and administrative power, and defends a communicative reason against the pessimism of the first Frankfurt School.
It is his main work, one of the great social theories of the late 20th century and the basis of his theory of deliberative democracy.

fuentes/la-etica-protestante/titulo.texto: The Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism

fuentes/la-etica-protestante/resumen.texto: Essay published in two parts in 1904 and 1905 in a social science journal that Weber co-edited. It argues that the ethic of ascetic Protestantism, above all of Calvinism and Puritanism, with the idea of work as a calling and the search for signs of salvation in a methodical life, favored the emergence of the spirit of modern capitalism. Weber makes clear that he does not claim to explain capitalism by religion alone.

fuentes/la-etica-protestante/por_que_imp.texto: It is one of the founding texts of sociology and one of the most debated: historians objected that capitalism existed earlier and outside the Protestant world. It is the source of the image of the “iron cage” of modern rationality.

fuentes/la-politica-como-vocacion/resume.texto: Lecture that Weber gave on 28 January 1919 to students in Munich, in the midst of the German Revolution, and published that same year. It defines the state as the human community that successfully claims the monopoly of the legitimate use of physical force within a territory, distinguishes three types of legitimate domination (traditional, charismatic and legal) and contrasts the ethic of conviction with the ethic of responsibility.

fuentes/la-politica-como-vocacion/por_qu.texto: Its definition of the state is one of the most cited in the social sciences, and the distinction between the two ethics remains a reference for thinking about politics.

fuentes/el-suicidio/resumen.texto: Study that uses statistics from several European countries to show that the suicide rate depends on social facts and not only on individual causes. It distinguishes egoistic, altruistic and anomic suicide according to the degree of integration and regulation of groups; for example, it finds more suicides among Protestants than among Catholics and Jews.

fuentes/el-suicidio/por_que_importa.texto: It is an early model of empirical sociological research and one of the texts that founded sociology as a discipline.

fuentes/curso-de-linguistica-general/res.texto: Posthumous book, published in 1916, put together by his disciples Charles Bally and Albert Sechehaye from students’ notes of the courses Saussure taught in Geneva between 1907 and 1911. It distinguishes language as a social system (langue) from individual speech (parole), defines the linguistic sign as the arbitrary union of a signifier and a signified, and proposes studying language at a given moment (synchrony) as well as its history (diachrony).

fuentes/curso-de-linguistica-general/por.texto: It founded structural linguistics and was the basis of structuralism, which in the 1960s spread to anthropology, literary criticism and philosophy.

fuentes/tristes-tropicos/resumen.texto: Book of travels and memoirs in which Lévi-Strauss recounts his stay in Brazil between 1935 and 1939, as a professor in São Paulo, and his expeditions to the Caduveo, the Bororo, the Nambikwara and the Tupi-Kawahib, together with reflections on civilization and travel. It opens with the sentence “I hate travelling and explorers”.

fuentes/tristes-tropicos/por_que_importa.texto: It brought anthropology to the general public and is one of the most widely read French non-fiction books of the century. The Académie Goncourt regretted being unable to award it a prize because it was not a novel.

fuentes/estructuras-sintacticas/resumen.texto: Short book in which Chomsky proposes describing a language by means of a generative grammar: a finite set of rules, including transformational rules, capable of producing all the grammatical sentences of the language and only those. His example “Colorless green ideas sleep furiously” shows that a sentence can be grammatical without making sense. It was published by Mouton in The Hague.

fuentes/estructuras-sintacticas/por_que_.texto: It began the so-called Chomskyan revolution in linguistics and was important for cognitive science and theoretical computer science.

fuentes/comprender-los-medios/resumen.texto: Essay that studies media, from writing and the printing press to radio and television, as extensions of the human senses and body that transform perception and society beyond their content. It contains the formula “the medium is the message” and the distinction between “hot” and “cool” media.

fuentes/comprender-los-medios/por_que_im.texto: It made McLuhan a celebrity and anticipated debates about television and the internet; his expression “global village”, coined shortly before, came into common use.

fuentes/propaganda-bernays/resumen.texto: Book in which Bernays openly defends the “conscious and intelligent manipulation of the organized habits and opinions of the masses” as a necessary element of democratic society, in the hands of an “invisible government” of experts. He explains with his own cases how to create events and use authority figures to influence the public on behalf of companies, causes and governments.

fuentes/propaganda-bernays/por_que_impor.texto: It is a founding text of public relations and one of the most cited by critics of the manipulation of public opinion. According to his memoirs, Bernays learned in 1933 that Goebbels had one of his books in his library.

fuentes/el-castillo/resumen.texto: Novel in which a man known only as K. arrives at a village to work as a land surveyor and fails to gain access to the authorities who govern it from a castle. Kafka began it on 27 January 1922, wrote most of it that year while convalescing from tuberculosis, and left the manuscript without an ending. Max Brod, his executor, published it in 1926, two years after Kafka's death and against Kafka's wish that his unpublished work be destroyed, with some editorial corrections.

fuentes/el-castillo/por_que_importa.texto: It is the last of Kafka's three novels, all unfinished and posthumous. It is usually read as a story about alienation and opaque bureaucracies that answer to no one, and it is one of the works that sustain the adjective “Kafkaesque.”

fuentes/america-kafka/resumen.texto: Novel that follows Karl Rossmann, a teenager sent to New York by his family, and his adventures in the United States. Kafka wrote it from 1911 and left it unfinished around 1914; its first chapter, “The Stoker,” was published separately in 1913. Kafka called it The Man Who Disappeared; the title Amerika was given by Max Brod, who gathered the manuscript and published it in 1927, after the author's death. Since 1982 it has also been published under its original title.

fuentes/america-kafka/por_que_importa.texto: It is Kafka's first novel and, like The Trial and The Castle, was left unfinished. It incorporates the experiences of relatives of his who had emigrated to the United States, a country Kafka never visited.

fuentes/america-kafka/leer.0.titulo.texto: First chapter (“Der Heizer,” “The Stoker”) in German, on Project Gutenberg

fuentes/en-la-colonia-penitenciaria/resu.texto: Story about a traveler who witnesses, in an unnamed penal colony, what may be the last execution by a machine that inscribes the text of the law the condemned man has broken onto his skin over twelve hours. An officer describes the apparatus and its justification while the traveler decides whether to intervene. Kafka wrote it in October 1914, revised it in November 1918, and it was published in October 1919; he read it aloud in public in Munich in 1916.

fuentes/en-la-colonia-penitenciaria/por_.texto: It was one of Kafka's texts published during his lifetime. After the atrocities of the 20th century it was read as an anticipation of bureaucratized violence and state terror, although it was written at the outset of World War I.

fuentes/en-la-colonia-penitenciaria/leer.texto: Original German text on Project Gutenberg

fuentes/la-condena/resumen.texto: Story about Georg Bendemann, a young merchant who writes to a friend in Russia to announce his engagement and argues with his father, who questions the friend's existence and ends by sentencing him to death by drowning. Kafka wrote it in a single sitting on 22 September 1912.

fuentes/la-condena/por_que_importa.texto: Kafka considered it one of his most accomplished creations. The theme of the relationship between father and son reappears in The Metamorphosis and in the Letter to His Father. It was published in 1913.

fuentes/la-condena/leer.0.titulo.texto: Original German text on Project Gutenberg

fuentes/un-medico-rural/resumen.texto: First-person story of a village doctor who is called out at night, in the depths of winter, to attend a sick boy in a distant village. Without a horse of his own, he is given two by a stableboy who emerges from a pigsty and throws himself at his maid Rosa. The doctor finds an open wound full of maggots in the boy's side; the villagers undress him and put him to bed beside the patient, and the doctor flees on a very slow return journey through the snow. Kafka wrote it in 1917; it appeared in 1918 in the almanac Die neue Dichtung, published by Kurt Wolff, and in 1920 it gave its title to his second collection of stories.

fuentes/un-medico-rural/por_que_importa.texto: Kafka considered it one of his few truly successful stories. In a letter to Max Brod from September 1917 he said that with the boy's wound he had “predicted” his illness, the tuberculosis that killed him.

fuentes/un-medico-rural/leer.0.titulo.texto: Original German text, in the book Ein Landarzt, on Project Gutenberg

fuentes/un-artista-del-hambre/resumen.texto: Story about a professional fasting performer who displays himself in a cage, whose art loses its audience until he dies almost forgotten and is replaced by a panther. It was published in 1922 in the magazine Die neue Rundschau. It gives its title to the last book Kafka prepared for the press, with three other stories, which appeared in 1924, shortly after his death.

fuentes/un-artista-del-hambre/por_que_im.texto: It is one of Kafka's late stories about the artist and his isolation from society. Hunger artists were a real spectacle at fairs and circuses between the late 19th and early 20th centuries.

fuentes/un-artista-del-hambre/leer.0.tit.texto: Original German text on Project Gutenberg

fuentes/el-lobo-estepario/resumen.texto: Novel presented as the papers of Harry Haller, a middle-aged man divided between his civilized side and his “steppenwolf” side, who feels alien to bourgeois society and passes through a magic theater of fantasy and self-examination. Hesse wrote it mainly at the Hotel Krafft in Basel (according to another source, he began it there and finished it in Zurich); fragments appeared in the magazine Neue Rundschau in 1926 and 1927, and the book came out in 1927 from the S. Fischer publishing house in Berlin. It reflects a personal crisis of the author in the 1920s.

fuentes/el-lobo-estepario/por_que_import.texto: Hesse later said the book had been misunderstood, because many readers saw only Haller's suffering and not the possibility of overcoming it.

fuentes/el-lobo-estepario/leer.0.titulo.texto: English translation (Project Gutenberg), public domain in the US

fuentes/el-lobo-estepario/leer.1.titulo.texto: German text “Der Steppenwolf” (Project Gutenberg), public domain in the US

fuentes/demian/resumen.texto: Coming-of-age novel narrated in the first person by Emil Sinclair, who from childhood moves from a world of orderly appearances to a darker one under the guidance of his companion Max Demian, who reinterprets Cain as a strong figure rather than a villain. Hesse wrote it in 1917 during psychoanalytic treatment with a disciple of Jung and published it in 1919 under the pseudonym Emil Sinclair; from the tenth edition onward it bears his name.

fuentes/demian/por_que_importa.texto: Under the pseudonym it won the Fontane Prize, reserved for debut authors, and Hesse returned it when his identity became known. It shows his contact with Jung's psychology and the theme of the search for individual identity.

fuentes/demian/leer.0.titulo.texto: English translation (Project Gutenberg), public domain in the US

fuentes/demian/leer.1.titulo.texto: German text (Project Gutenberg), public domain in the US

fuentes/el-juego-de-los-abalorios/resume.texto: Novel set in a distant future, in the fictional province of Castalia, where an intellectual elite practices the Glass Bead Game, which combines music, mathematics and other disciplines. It narrates the life of Josef Knecht, who becomes Magister Ludi and ends by questioning the isolation of his order. Hesse began it in 1931 in Switzerland, and it was published in Zurich in 1943, after an edition for Germany had been refused because of the author's antifascist ideas. It was his last novel.

fuentes/el-juego-de-los-abalorios/por_qu.texto: It was the last novel Hesse published in his lifetime, three years before he received the Nobel Prize in Literature (1946). The imaginary game in the novel inspired designers of real games.

fuentes/narciso-y-goldmundo/resumen.texto: Novel about the friendship between Narcissus, a monk and teacher at the school of the Mariabronn monastery, and Goldmundo, a pupil who leaves the cloister and wanders through Germany at the end of the Middle Ages, among love, art and the plague, until he is reunited with his friend. Hesse wrote it between April 1927 and March 1929 and published it in 1930 with the S. Fischer publishing house in Berlin.

fuentes/narciso-y-goldmundo/por_que_impo.texto: It sets the life of the spirit against that of the senses as two paths that complement each other. On publication it was regarded as a literary triumph for Hesse.

fuentes/peter-camenzind/resumen.texto: Hesse's first novel. It follows a young peasant with autobiographical traits who goes to the city to become a poet. It was serialized in the magazine Neue Rundschau between October and December 1903 and published as a book in January 1904 by the S. Fischer publishing house in Berlin.

fuentes/peter-camenzind/por_que_importa.texto: It brought Hesse fame. It raises themes he later returned to: the search for identity, nature versus civilization, and the role of art.

fuentes/peter-camenzind/leer.0.titulo.texto: German text (Project Gutenberg), public domain in the US

fuentes/bajo-las-ruedas/resumen.texto: Novel about Hans Giebenrath, a brilliant pupil who enters a demanding Protestant seminary, breaks down under the pressure and ends up outside the system. It was serialized in the Neue Zürcher Zeitung in 1904 and published as a book by the S. Fischer publishing house in Berlin at the end of 1905, with an imprint date of 1906. It has autobiographical traits: Hesse left the seminary at Maulbronn.

fuentes/bajo-las-ruedas/por_que_importa.texto: It is a critique of an education that prioritizes performance over personal development, a constant theme in Hesse's work.

fuentes/bajo-las-ruedas/leer.0.titulo.texto: German text “Unterm Rad” (Project Gutenberg), public domain in the US

fuentes/la-caida/resumen.texto: Short novel made up of the monologues of Jean-Baptiste Clamence, a former Parisian lawyer who, in an Amsterdam bar, presents himself as a “penitent judge” and tells a stranger about the crisis that led him from a respected life to the confession of his guilt. Gallimard published it in Paris in 1956, a year before Camus received the Nobel Prize in Literature. It is the last novel Camus published.

fuentes/la-caida/por_que_importa.texto: It deals with guilt and the judgment of others. It was originally intended for the short story collection Exile and the Kingdom (1957), which was published later.

fuentes/el-hombre-rebelde/resumen.texto: Essay examining metaphysical and historical rebellion in Western thought and art, distinguishing the rebellion that affirms a limit from the revolutions that, in Camus's view, justify crime in the name of history. It was published in 1951. Marxists and Sartre criticized it; Francis Jeanson criticized it in Les Temps modernes, Sartre's magazine, in 1952; Camus replied, and Sartre's response sealed the break between the two.

fuentes/el-hombre-rebelde/por_que_import.texto: It fixes Camus's political and moral position toward Soviet communism. It continues The Myth of Sisyphus, which dealt with the absurd.

fuentes/caligula-camus/resumen.texto: Play about the Roman emperor Caligula who, after the death of his sister and lover Drusilla, decides to exercise unlimited freedom and ends up murdered in a conspiracy. Camus began it in 1938 (the first manuscript is from 1939), and Gallimard published it in May 1944; it premiered on 26 September 1945 at the Théâtre Hébertot in Paris, with Gérard Philipe. He revised it several times afterward.

fuentes/caligula-camus/por_que_importa.texto: Together with The Stranger and The Myth of Sisyphus, it forms Camus's “cycle of the absurd.”

fuentes/a-puerta-cerrada/resumen.texto: Play in which three dead people, Garcin, Inès and Estelle, are locked together in a room that is their hell, with no torturers: each depends on the gaze of the others. It premiered in May 1944 at the Théâtre du Vieux-Colombier in Paris, during the German occupation.

fuentes/a-puerta-cerrada/por_que_importa.texto: It contains the phrase “Hell is other people,” widely quoted as a summary of Sartre's idea of the gaze of others, which fixes the subject.

fuentes/las-moscas-sartre/resumen.texto: Play that reworks the myth of Electra and Orestes: Orestes returns to Argos, kills his mother Clytemnestra and Aegisthus, who had murdered Agamemnon, and accepts his act without remorse while the Erinyes, the flies of the title, pursue him. It premiered in 1943 in Paris, under German occupation.

fuentes/las-moscas-sartre/por_que_import.texto: It presents in dramatic form Sartre's idea of freedom and of responsibility for one's own act.

fuentes/las-manos-sucias/resumen.texto: Political drama set in the fictional Illyria between 1943 and 1945, which tells in flashback how a young communist, Hugo, murdered a leader of his own party who proposed making a pact with other forces. It raises the tension between ideals and political action that forces one to “get one's hands dirty.” It premiered on 2 April 1948 at the Théâtre Antoine in Paris.

fuentes/las-manos-sucias/por_que_importa.texto: It is Sartre's most debated work on politics. The French Communist Party attacked it for presenting a communist leader in that situation, and Sartre rejected the charge that it was anticommunist.

fuentes/las-palabras-sartre/resumen.texto: Sartre's autobiography of childhood, in two parts, “Reading” and “Writing,” in which he recounts his discovery of books and his literary vocation in his maternal grandfather's house. It appeared in 1963 in Les Temps modernes and as a book in 1964, the year Sartre declined the Nobel Prize in Literature.

fuentes/las-palabras-sartre/por_que_impo.texto: In it Sartre distances himself from literature and from his own vocation. Critics received it almost unanimously as a literary success.

fuentes/corazon-de-perro/resumen.texto: Satire on Professor Preobrazhensky, who transplants the pituitary gland and testicles of a man into a stray dog and creates Poligraph Poligraphovich Sharikov, a crude being who becomes a functionary of the regime. Bulgakov wrote it in 1925, during the New Economic Policy (NEP). Its publication was rejected that year, it circulated in clandestine copies, and it was officially published in the Soviet Union in 1987.

fuentes/corazon-de-perro/por_que_importa.texto: It is read as an allegory of the revolution and of the attempt to transform human beings by force. Its 1988 television version had a great impact in the Soviet Union.

fuentes/la-guardia-blanca/resumen.texto: Novel about the Turbin family, members of the Kyiv intelligentsia, trapped between the armies contending for the city during the civil war after 1917, in which Whites, Reds, Germans and Ukrainian nationalists under Petliura fought over Kyiv, with Hetman Skoropadsky as the backdrop. It was serialized in the magazine Rossiya in 1925, but the magazine closed before it was finished; the complete novel came out in Paris, in two volumes, in 1927 and 1929, and was reissued in the Soviet Union only in 1966, in a censored version.

fuentes/la-guardia-blanca/por_que_import.texto: Bulgakov adapted it for the stage as The Days of the Turbins, which premiered in 1926. It is his first novel.

fuentes/huevos-fatales/resumen.texto: Short satirical science fiction novella set in Moscow in 1928, then a near future. The zoologist Persikov discovers a red ray that accelerates the development of embryos; an official uses it on chicken eggs and, by mistake, on reptile eggs, and a plague of giant beasts threatens the capital. Bulgakov finished it in early October 1924; it appeared in 1925 in the almanac Nedra (no. 6) and that same year in the book Diaboliad.

fuentes/huevos-fatales/por_que_importa.texto: Many Soviet critics read it as a mockery of the 1917 Revolution and the Soviet leadership. It was popular at the time.

fuentes/tres-camaradas/resumen.texto: Novel narrated in the first person by Robert Lohkamp, a veteran of World War I who runs a car repair shop with his friends Otto Köster and Gottfried Lenz in an unnamed German city, between 1928 and 1929, and who falls in love with Patricia Hollmann, who is ill with tuberculosis. Remarque wrote it in exile. It first appeared in Danish translation (1936) and in English (1937), and in German in 1938, from the Querido publishing house in Amsterdam; in Germany it was not published until 1951.

fuentes/tres-camaradas/por_que_importa.texto: It portrays unemployment, political violence and the disillusionment of the postwar generation in Germany before Nazism. It continues the theme of the wartime generation that Remarque had already treated in All Quiet on the Western Front.

fuentes/arco-de-triunfo/resumen.texto: Novel about Ravic, a German refugee surgeon without papers in Paris, who operates for French doctors who exploit him, awaits expulsion, and falls in love with an actress of Italian origin, Joan Madou, on the eve of World War II. Remarque wrote it during his exile in the United States (1939-1948). It first appeared in English in 1945 (serialized in Collier's and as a book by Appleton-Century) and in German in 1946, in Zurich.

fuentes/arco-de-triunfo/por_que_importa.texto: It is his second great worldwide success, after All Quiet on the Western Front. It shows the situation of stateless refugees fleeing Nazism.

fuentes/el-obelisco-negro/resumen.texto: Novel narrated by Ludwig Bodmer, a gravestone seller in the fictional town of Werdenbrück, in 1923, during German hyperinflation. It portrays World War I veterans who fail to achieve a normal life; its subtitle is “The Story of a Belated Youth.” Remarque wrote it while living in Switzerland and published it in 1956, based on notes from the 1920s and 1930s.

fuentes/el-obelisco-negro/por_que_import.texto: It continues the thematic thread of All Quiet on the Western Front and The Road Back, about the survivors of the war in the Weimar Republic.

fuentes/nieve-pamuk/resumen.texto: Novel in which Ka, a Turkish poet exiled in Germany, returns to Turkey and travels to the city of Kars, isolated by snowfall, where he investigates a series of suicides of young girls and witnesses a local coup d'état, amid a clash between Islamists, secularists and nationalists. It was published in Turkish in 2002 and in English in 2004. The suicides have a real basis in events that occurred in Kars.

fuentes/nieve-pamuk/por_que_importa.texto: It is Pamuk's most explicitly political novel and deals with the cultural and political tensions of modern Turkey.

fuentes/el-museo-de-la-inocencia/resumen.texto: Novel set in Istanbul between 1975 and 1984 about the love of Kemal, a well-off businessman, for his distant relative Füsun, from a poorer family, and about his obsession with collecting objects connected to her. It was published on 29 August 2008. Among other themes, it deals with the condition of women in Turkish society of those years.

fuentes/el-museo-de-la-inocencia/por_que.texto: In 2012 Pamuk opened a real museum with that name in the Çukurcuma neighborhood of Istanbul, with objects evoking everyday life in the city in the period of the novel.

fuentes/el-castillo-blanco/resumen.texto: Novel set in Ottoman Istanbul in the 17th century about a young Venetian scholar captured by Ottoman soldiers while traveling to Naples, and his relationship with his Turkish master, who physically resembles him. It was published in Turkish in 1985.

fuentes/el-castillo-blanco/por_que_impor.texto: It deals with identity and the encounter between East and West through two men who become confused with each other.

fuentes/historia-de-la-filosofia-occiden.texto: Study of Western philosophy from the Presocratics to the early 20th century, in which each major section is preceded by an overview of its historical context. Russell wrote it between 1940 and 1943, living mainly in Pennsylvania, based on lectures he gave at the Barnes Foundation in Philadelphia in 1941 and 1942; it was published in 1945 in the United States and in 1946 in the United Kingdom. It was criticized for its generalizations.
It was a great commercial success and was cited among the works for which Russell received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1950. It gave him financial stability in his last years.

fuentes/por-que-no-soy-cristiano/titulo.texto: Why I Am Not a Christian

fuentes/por-que-no-soy-cristiano/resumen.texto: Essay based on a lecture Russell gave on 6 March 1927 at the Battersea Town Hall in London, at the invitation of the South London branch of the National Secular Society. It was published that year as a pamphlet. Russell questions the traditional arguments for the existence of God and the moral figure of Christ, and holds that religion rests mainly on fear. It was later reprinted in a 1957 collection of essays with the same title.

fuentes/por-que-no-soy-cristiano/por_que.texto: It is one of Russell's most widely circulated texts on religion. The New York Public Library included it among the most important books of the 20th century.

fuentes/los-problemas-de-la-filosofia/re.texto: Brief introduction to philosophy published in 1912, which presents the discipline as repeated attempts to answer the same questions: whether an external world can be proven, causation, the validity of generalizations, or an objective morality. Russell holds that philosophy does not resolve them and that its value lies elsewhere.

fuentes/los-problemas-de-la-filosofia/po.texto: It sets out Russell's theory of knowledge, including his distinction between knowledge by acquaintance and knowledge by description.

fuentes/los-problemas-de-la-filosofia/le.texto: English text on Project Gutenberg (public domain in the United States)

fuentes/dublineses/resumen.texto: Collection of fifteen stories about the life of Dublin's middle and lower classes at the beginning of the 20th century. Joyce wrote them between 1904 and 1907. From 1905, when he sent a first manuscript to a publisher, until its publication on 15 June 1914, he submitted it eighteen times to fifteen publishers; several objected to its content and demanded changes. It portrays the cultural and moral “paralysis” of the city and closes with “The Dead.”

fuentes/dublineses/por_que_importa.texto: It is Joyce's first book of fiction and the origin of his portrait of Dublin, which continues in Ulysses. It was written at the height of Irish nationalism, which Joyce saw as another factor in that paralysis.

fuentes/luz-de-agosto/resumen.texto: Novel set in the American South in the 1930s, in the fictional Yoknapatawpha County. It intertwines the stories of Lena Grove, a young pregnant woman who seeks the father of her child, and Joe Christmas, a man who believes he has Black ancestry but passes for white. Faulkner began the text in 1931 under the title “Dark House,” and it was published in 1932.

fuentes/luz-de-agosto/por_que_importa.texto: It is one of the four major novels of Faulkner's early period, along with The Sound and the Fury, As I Lay Dying and Absalom, Absalom! It deals with racism, identity and religion in the segregated South.

fuentes/absalon-absalon/resumen.texto: Novel that tells the rise and fall of Thomas Sutpen, born poor in western Virginia, who settles in Mississippi to found a plantation and a dynasty, before, during and after the Civil War. It is narrated by several unreliable witnesses years later. It was published in 1936.

fuentes/absalon-absalon/por_que_importa.texto: Its title refers to the rebellious son of King David in the Bible.
